  WHY: Explicitly opted-in issues enter the Claude queue without a pickup session to start implementation, so they stay unimplemented until the queue watchdog alerts.

  WHY: The queue has no pickup session to start implementation, so issues stay unimplemented until the queue watchdog alerts.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:58-59 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The routing-order docstring still documents the old Claude-default behavior: "6. repository variable AI_ISSUE_IMPLEMENTER: codex -> codex; empty or claude -> claude; anything else -> claude with a warning". The PR implementation already changed DEFAULT_IMPLEMENTER to IMPLEMENTER_CODEX on line 90, so the documented contract contradicts the actual routing logic.
  WHY: The code routes correctly, but every reader of the module docstring learns the wrong default and invalid-fallback behavior. An operator who reads only the docstring and not the implementation will believe unset or invalid AI_ISSUE_IMPLEMENTER routes issues to Claude.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:415-419 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The YAML comment says "Standalone issues default to the Claude issue implementer; set the repo variable to codex to keep the Codex clarify -> plan -> implement pipeline." After Phase 0, standalone issues default to Codex, and setting the variable to claude routes to Claude. The comment now gives operators the opposite instruction from reality.
  WHY: The routing logic is correct, but the comment misleads any operator reading the workflow. The warning text on line 487 was updated to say "(codex)" as the default, so the two comments within the same step now contradict each other.
- README.md:1216-1218 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The section still opens with "Standalone issues — anything the AI orchestrator does not manage — are implemented by Claude Code by default, in every repository that runs ai-clarify.yml (every install profile)." After Phase 0, standalone issues default to the Codex pipeline, and Claude is opt-in via label or repo variable.
  WHY: The routing behavior is correct, but this section is the primary operator-facing documentation for issue routing. Every new operator who reads it will believe new issues go to Claude and may configure their repo or labels around a wrong assumption. The table at line 1321 was updated to show Codex as the default, but the section introduction above it still says the opposite.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- changelog.d/6118-phase-0-standalone-issues-default-to-codex.md:7 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The lead paragraph states the Claude routing path still works for an explicit `ai:claude` label or `AI_ISSUE_IMPLEMENTER=claude` var, but the PR description records that the operator deleted every automation Routine and archived every implementation session, so the `claude-issue-intake.yml` → `ai:clarude-issue-queue` → pickup → `/implement-issue-claude` chain has no consumer for the queue: the issue is labelled and the dispatch fires, but no implementation session is ever started, and the issue sits open until the watchdog alerts or someone moves it to Codex by hand.
  WHY: A repo that follows the changelog's instruction and sets `AI_ISSUE_IMPLEMENTER=claude` (or a user who labels an issue `ai:claude`) believes they have opted back into Claude. The route returns `claude` with reason `repo_var` or `label_override`, the intake queues the issue, and nothing implements it. The fragment presents the path as "still routes to Claude while that path exists", but the path no longer exists end-to-end.
